Item 16 ("space 3.") is a sentence end but on a number, which was strong in the data, so I called it firing with low confidence.

turn1.explanation: The unit fires on the token immediately before a period '.', and fires hardest when that period is internal to a larger token sequence rather than ending a sentence. Typical strong cases are decimal points (0.07, 29.9), URL or domain dots (www., github.com), code member access (target.nodeName, params.delete) and abbreviation dots (N.C., U.S., R. 47.5).
turn1.evidence: Every marked token directly precedes a '.': '-0|10'.07, 'www|10'.aace, 'classList|10'.toggle, 'N|10'.C., '2|9'.000m2 and 'U|10'.S. Sentence-final words get weaker activations ('have|6'., 'gaming|6'., 'etc|5'.), with one exception: 'recognized|9'. has no space after its period, which fits the idea that a dot-joined continuation is what drives strong firing.
